chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Group III-A and Group IV-A Elements
title: Chapter 3: Group III-A and Group IV-A Elements
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of Borax?
questions.explanation: Borax is sodium tetraborate decahydrate, structurally written as Na₂[B₄O₅(OH)₄] · 8H₂O.

questions.question: In the Borax bead test, a cobalt salt heated on a platinum wire loop in an oxidizing flame produces a characteristic bead of which color?
questions.explanation: Cobalt metaborate [Co(BO₂)₂] forms a characteristic deep blue glassy bead.

questions.question: Orthoboric acid (H₃BO₃) behaves in aqueous solution as:

options.A: A strong tribasic protonic Arrhenius acid
options.B: A weak monobasic Lewis acid accepting an OH⁻ ion from water

questions.explanation: B(OH)₃ does not donate its own protons; instead it accepts OH⁻: B(OH)₃ + 2H₂O ⇌ [B(OH)₄]⁻ + H₃O⁺ (monobasic Lewis acid).

questions.question: In diborane (B₂H₆), the two bridging B-H-B bonds are best described as:
questions.explanation: Each bridge bond involves two boron atoms and one bridging hydrogen sharing only 2 electrons, known as a 3c-2e banana bond.

questions.question: Why is Lead(II) oxide (PbO) more stable than Lead(IV) oxide (PbO₂)?

options.A: Electronegativity of Pb is lower than Carbon
options.B: Inert pair effect makes the +2 oxidation state far more stable for heavy Pb than +4
options.C: PbO is a gas at room temperature

questions.explanation: Due to poor shielding by 4f¹⁴ and 5d¹⁰ electrons, the 6s² electrons remain unshared (inert pair effect); thus Pb²⁺ is much more stable than Pb⁴⁺.

questions.question: Potash alum, used widely in water purification and mordanting, has the formula:
questions.explanation: Potash alum is potassium aluminum sulfate dodecahydrate dimer: K₂SO₄ · Al₂(SO₄)₃ · 24H₂O.

questions.question: The exceptional hardness and high melting point (>3500°C) of diamond is attributed to:

options.A: Van der Waals forces between graphene layers
options.B: Giant three-dimensional tetrahedral network of sp³-hybridized carbon atoms linked by strong covalent bonds

questions.explanation: Every carbon in diamond is sp³ hybridized, bonded tetrahedrally to 4 other carbons in an interlocking 3D covalent lattice.

questions.question: Graphite conducts electricity parallel to its layers because:

options.B: Each carbon atom is sp² hybridized, leaving one unhybridized 2p electron per atom delocalized over the hexagonal sheet

questions.explanation: Delocalized π-electrons in the planar sp² hexagonal rings move freely parallel to the sheets under an applied voltage.

questions.question: What is the common chemical name of 'water glass'?
questions.explanation: Sodium silicate (Na₂SiO₃) dissolves in water to form a viscous alkaline liquid known as water glass.

questions.question: Silicones are synthetic polymers characterized by which repeating backbone unit?
questions.explanation: Silicones (polyorganosiloxanes) consist of repeating -[R₂Si-O]- units with high thermal stability and water-repellent properties.

questions.question: White lead, a historic white pigment in oil paints, chemically corresponds to:
questions.explanation: White lead is basic lead carbonate [2PbCO₃ · Pb(OH)₂].

questions.question: Red lead (Sindoor / Minium), used in anti-corrosive primer paints for iron and steel, has the formula:
questions.explanation: Trilead tetraoxide (Pb₃O₄), considered a mixed oxide 2PbO·PbO₂, is red lead.

questions.question: In the Hall-Héroult industrial process for the extraction of aluminum, cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is added to molten alumina (Al₂O₃) to:

options.A: Lower the melting point from 2050°C to ~950°C and improve electrical conductivity

questions.explanation: Cryolite dissolves Al₂O₃, depressing its melting point from over 2000°C to ~950°C and providing ionic conductivity.

questions.question: Carbon monoxide (CO) is extremely poisonous to humans because:

options.A: It destroys red blood cells directly
options.B: It binds to hemoglobin ~250 times more strongly than oxygen, forming carboxyhemoglobin and causing cellular hypoxia
options.C: It produces carbonic acid in tissues

questions.explanation: CO forms stable carboxyhemoglobin, blocking O₂ delivery to tissues and causing asphyxiation.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds exhibits a 3-center 2-electron bond analogous to diborane?
questions.explanation: Al₂(CH₃)₆ contains bridging methyl groups forming 3c-2e Al-C-Al bonds to compensate for aluminum's octet deficiency.

questions.question: An aqueous solution of borax is alkaline to litmus because of:

options.A: Complete ionization into strong base NaOH and weak acid H₃BO₃ upon hydrolysis

questions.explanation: Na₂B₄O₇ + 7H₂O ⇌ 2NaOH (strong base) + 4H₃BO₃ (weak acid); high [OH⁻] renders the solution distinctly alkaline (pH ~9).

questions.question: Which of the following is the most powerful Lewis acid among boron trihalides?
questions.explanation: In BF₃, effective 2pπ-2pπ back-bonding reduces the electron deficiency of boron. In BI₃, 2p-5p back-bonding is ineffective, making BI₃ the strongest Lewis acid.

questions.question: Which gas is liberated when aluminum metal dissolves in warm aqueous sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.explanation: 2 Al + 2 NaOH + 6 H₂O → 2 Na[Al(OH)₄] + 3 H₂↑. Aluminum is amphoteric and reacts with strong bases to liberate H₂.

questions.question: Tin exists in two allotropic forms: white tin (metallic β-tin) and grey tin (non-metallic α-tin). The crumbly disintegration of tin objects in freezing weather is called:
questions.explanation: Below 13.2°C, white metallic β-tin slowly converts to brittle, grey powdery α-tin with lower density, known as tin pest.

questions.question: The Thermite process, used in welding railway tracks, utilizes the vigorous exothermic redox reaction between:
questions.explanation: 2 Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2 Fe (molten) + massive heat (~3000°C), sufficient to fuse steel rails.

questions.question: What is the geometry of the silicon tetrachloride (SiCl₄) molecule?
questions.explanation: Silicon is sp³ hybridized with four bonded chlorine atoms and zero lone pairs, giving a regular tetrahedral geometry.

questions.question: Fullerenes (such as C₆₀, Buckminsterfullerene) consist of carbon atoms arranged in:

options.A: A spherical cage of 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons

questions.explanation: C₆₀ resembles a soccer ball with 12 five-membered rings and 20 six-membered rings of sp²-hybridized carbon atoms.

questions.question: Aluminum utensils are protected against atmospheric corrosion by a tenacious self-healing surface film of:
questions.explanation: A dense, non-porous layer of aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃) immediately passivates the metal surface against further oxidation.

questions.question: Which of the following elements in Group IVA has the greatest catenation capability?
questions.explanation: Carbon forms exceptionally strong C-C single bonds (347 kJ/mol) due to small atomic size and optimal orbital overlap.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is an active ingredient in eye lotions and talcum powders due to its mild antiseptic properties?
questions.explanation: Boric acid (H₃BO₃) is a gentle non-irritating antiseptic used in eye washes and baby dusting powders.

questions.question: What is the oxidation state of lead in lead dioxide (PbO₂)?
questions.explanation: In PbO₂, each oxide ion is O²⁻; hence Pb is in the +4 oxidation state, making it a strong oxidizing agent.

questions.question: Which chloride is an electron-deficient dimer in the vapor phase, existing as Al₂Cl₆?
questions.explanation: In vapor or nonpolar solvents, AlCl₃ dimerizes to Al₂Cl₆ where chlorine atoms donate lone pairs into empty Al 3p orbitals.

questions.question: What happens when orthoboric acid (H₃BO₃) is heated to red heat (>160°C)?

options.B: It decomposes completely to form glassy Boric Oxide (B₂O₃)

questions.explanation: H₃BO₃ → HBO₂ (metaboric acid at 100°C) → H₂B₄O₇ (tetraboric acid at 160°C) → B₂O₃ (boron trioxide / boric anhydride at red heat).

questions.question: Which form of silica is used as a desiccant (drying agent) in laboratories and packaging?
questions.explanation: Silica gel is an amorphous porous form of SiO₂ with high specific surface area, readily adsorbing water vapor.

questions.question: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a gas at room temperature while silicon dioxide (SiO₂) is a high-melting solid because:

options.A: CO₂ is non-polar but SiO₂ is ionic
options.B: C forms discrete linear molecules with pπ-pπ double bonds (O=C=O), while Si cannot form effective pπ-pπ bonds and forms a giant covalent 3D network of single Si-O bonds
options.C: Silicon has lower electronegativity than Oxygen

questions.explanation: Larger 3p orbitals of Si cannot overlap laterally to form stable π bonds; Si forms four single Si-O bonds in a giant 3D quartz lattice.

questions.question: Which of the following Group IVA oxides is amphoteric?
questions.explanation: SnO₂ (and PbO₂) react with both strong acids and strong alkalis (forming stannates [Sn(OH)₆]²⁻), displaying amphoteric behavior.

questions.question: The poisonous gas phosgene (carbonyl chloride, COCl₂) is produced by the slow photochemical oxidation of:
questions.explanation: 2 CHCl₃ + O₂ (in light) → 2 COCl₂ + 2 HCl. Hence chloroform bottles are tinted brown and filled to the brim.

questions.question: Which of the following is an organosilicon compound used as a water-repellent coating and surgical lubricant?
questions.explanation: Silicones possess hydrocarbon organic side groups pointing outwards, providing hydrophobicity, biocompatibility, and chemical inertness.

questions.question: Silicon carbide (SiC), known commercially as Carborundum, is widely used as:

options.B: An industrial abrasive and cutting tool material due to diamond-like hardness

questions.explanation: Carborundum (SiC) has a 3D covalent tetrahedral structure with Mohs hardness ~9.5, making it an excellent abrasive.

questions.question: Why does aluminum not react with concentrated nitric acid (HNO₃)?

options.A: Nitric acid is too weak to attack aluminum
options.B: Concentrated HNO₃ is a powerful oxidizing agent that renders aluminum passive by forming an impervious oxide film (Al₂O₃)
options.C: Aluminum is below hydrogen in the electrochemical series

questions.explanation: Concentrated HNO₃ immediately passivates aluminum metal by generating a protective, insoluble, non-reactive film of Al₂O₃.
